title: Aloysius Gonzaga (21 June)
hookLine: a young Jesuit who died nursing plague victims in Rome

lines: A YOUNG MAN LIFTS A STRANGER.
cards: Rome, during an epidemic, and the hospitals are crowded. The story goes that a young Jesuit stoops to lift a sick man off the street and carry him inside. He's a student, not yet a priest.
Not long before, he was the heir of a princely family, trained to be a soldier. Today, Aloysius Gonzaga.

teach.b: Aloysius was born into the Gonzagas, a powerful noble family in northern Italy, the eldest son and heir. His father wanted a soldier and a prince, and trained him for it. Aloysius wanted something else.
Tradition says he was serious about prayer from childhood, and that as a teenager at court he decided to join the Jesuits. His father fought it for a long time.
In the end Aloysius signed away his inheritance to his younger brother and walked into the Jesuit novitiate in Rome with nothing that marked him as a prince. Then came the epidemic.
Rome was full of the sick, and the Jesuits went out to nurse them. Aloysius asked to go. He washed and fed the sick, made their beds, carried them.
One story told about him is that he found a man collapsed in the street, lifted him onto his shoulders and brought him to the hospital.

He caught the disease himself, and after a long illness he died, still young, still a student, not yet a priest. Jesus describes the judgment of the nations, and among the things the righteous did, he lists this.
In the Douay-Rheims: "sick, and you visited me." Aloysius took it literally, and it cost him his life.
Pictures often show him with a lily, a sign of purity, and a pale, pious face that can make him look fragile.
The story says something tougher: a young man who stood up to a powerful father, gave away a fortune, and walked toward a disease many were running from.
The Church named him a patron of young people, and the story behind the title isn't gentleness. It's a young man, and a brave one.

how: The Church keeps the memorial of Saint Aloysius Gonzaga on 21 June; Jesuit schools and parishes often mark it, and he is honored as a patron of young people and students.

games.q: you're a young Jesuit student in Rome. an epidemic fills the streets with the sick. what do you do?
o: stay inside and pray for them.
ask to go out and nurse them.
leave the city until it passes.
games.why: Aloysius asked to nurse the sick, carried at least one man in from the street, caught the disease and died.

practice: Bring to mind someone who is ill right now, at home or in a hospital, and then the people caring for them: a nurse on a long shift, a parent up at night, an aide nobody thanks. Hold both.
If you pray, ask Saint Aloysius to stay close to them; if you don't, simply hold them with care.

wordCard.voice: Aloysius Gonzaga. The heir who gave up a princely life to be a Jesuit, and died young after nursing the sick of Rome.

carryVoice: Your line: young and brave. A lily on a holy card can hide a lot of courage. See you tomorrow.
